posts.title: Same task, two prompts, wildly different results

slides.title: A CLIENT SAID I WAS TOO EXPENSIVE. I ASKED AI TO REPLY
slides.kicker: One real task, start to finish

slides.heading: The message
slides.body: Friday afternoon. A client I wanted replies to my quote: this is way above our budget, can you do it for half? Every freelancer knows this exact stomach drop.
slides.engage: COMMENT YES IF YOU HAVE HAD THIS MESSAGE

slides.label: Attempt 1, the lazy brief
slides.prompt: Write a reply to a client who says I am too expensive.
slides.output: Thank you so much for your feedback! I completely understand budget concerns. I would be happy to offer you a discount to make this work...
slides.note: It folded instantly. No role, no stakes, no voice. The AI mirrored the effort I gave it.

slides.label: Attempt 2, the real brief
slides.prompt: You are a pricing coach for freelancers. A client I respect says my quote is double their budget. Write a reply that holds my price, offers a smaller scope instead of a discount, and sounds like me: warm, direct, no begging.
slides.output: I hear you on budget. Rather than cutting the price of the full project, here is what I can deliver properly at your number: the logo and one brand application. The full identity stays available when the budget does...
slides.note: Same AI. It held the price, protected the relationship and gave the client a real option.

slides.heading: Why this works
slides.body: AI is a pattern machine. A vague brief points it at the average of the internet, and the internet's average reply is a beggy discount. A precise brief points it at the exact conversation you are actually in.

slides.heading: Be honest
slides.a: The discount reply. Keep the client happy, win the job.
slides.b: The scope reply. Hold the price, offer less for less.
slides.ask: Which would you actually send? A or B in the comments. No judgement, real talk.

slides.heading: Steal the structure
slides.body: Role it should play. Situation with real details pasted in. Rules for tone and what not to do. Three sentences of brief buys you a reply you can send.

posts.title: The AI fluency quiz

slides.title: MOST PEOPLE SCORE 2 OUT OF 4 ON THIS

slides.heading: The rules
slides.body: Four questions. Guess each answer out loud before you swipe. Count your score honestly, and drop it in the comments at the end. No scrolling back.

slides.q: Why does AI sometimes state completely false things with total confidence?
slides.hint: Question 1 of 4. Lock in your answer, then swipe.

slides.heading: It predicts, it does not know
slides.body: AI generates the most likely next words, not verified facts. When it lacks the answer, the most likely words still look like an answer. That is a hallucination.
slides.why: Never trust names, numbers, prices or quotes without checking. Confidence is not accuracy.

slides.q: Why does a long chat slowly get dumber the longer it runs?
slides.hint: Question 2 of 4. This one catches everyone.

slides.heading: The context window filled up
slides.body: Everything in your chat lives in a short term memory with a hard size limit. When it fills, the oldest details fall out first, usually your original instructions.
slides.why: One chat, one job. Start fresh for a new task and re paste what matters.

slides.q: You ask for a 1000 word article and it stops at around 700. What happened?
slides.hint: Question 3 of 4. Hint: AI does not count words.

slides.heading: It ran out of tokens, not ideas
slides.body: AI reads and writes in tokens, chunks of roughly three quarters of a word, with limits per reply. It also cannot count words while writing, it estimates.
slides.why: Ask for structure instead of word counts: five sections, three paragraphs each. Structure it can obey.

slides.heading: This is how AI sees a sentence
slides.note: Nine tokens, six words. The orange chunks are whole words, the grey ones are word pieces. Every limit you hit is counted in these.

slides.q: What is the difference between a chatbot and an agent?
slides.hint: Last one. This word is about to be everywhere.

slides.heading: A chatbot answers, an agent acts
slides.body: An agent takes steps on its own: browsing, writing files, running tools, checking its work, finishing a job while you are away. The posts on this page are made by one every morning.
slides.why: Agents are why AI skills compound now. You stop doing tasks and start directing them.

slides.heading: SCORE OUT OF 4?
slides.body: Drop your honest score in the comments. Tag someone who thinks AI fluency is just typing questions. Tomorrow: the ten minute test that picks your AI for you.

posts.caption:

posts.title: Why your prompts fail

slides.title: YOUR PROMPTS FAIL BECAUSE AI IS A MIRROR

slides.heading: What AI actually does
slides.body: It completes patterns. Your prompt selects which patterns from everything it has read. A vague prompt selects the average of the internet, and the average of the internet is mediocre by definition.

slides.heading: Watch one prompt grow up
slides.body: Real task from my week: an Instagram bio. Version one is what most people type.
slides.example: v1: Write me an Instagram bio. Result: Passionate creative bringing your vision to life. Generic poison.

slides.heading: Version two: role and facts
slides.body: A role narrows the pattern space. Facts pin it to your world.
slides.example: v2: You are a bio writer for creatives. I am a graphic designer in SA, I do branding and social media, clients book me on WhatsApp. Result: usable but stiff.

slides.heading: Version three: rules and taste
slides.body: Format forces decisions. Bans kill the cliches you hate.
slides.example: v3: add. . . 5 options under 150 characters, plain confident language, no word passionate, no emoji soup. Result: the bio in my profile right now.

slides.heading: The formula hiding in there
slides.body: Role, then task with your real context, then format and rules. Three sentences minimum. And the first answer is a draft: say what is wrong and go again. Two rounds beats one perfect prompt.

slides.heading: The 5 minute upgrade
slides.body: Take one prompt you typed this week. Rewrite it with role, context, format. Run both versions side by side.
slides.action: Comment your before and after. Best upgrade gets featured on my story.

slides.heading: WEEK ONE DONE
slides.body: Seven posts, all receipts, zero recycled tips. Save the ones you will use, and follow: week two opens with the seven Claude features almost nobody uses.

posts.caption:
